title: AMD Debuts 6th Gen EPYC Verano CPU for AI Agent Scaling
summary:
The new 'Verano' data center processor featuring an LPDDR memory interface will be available in 2027 to support large-scale agentic AI deployments, AMD CEO Lisa Su announced at the OCP 2026 Global Summit. This 6th Gen EPYC chip is designed to address memory bandwidth constraints during AI training and inference. Su stated that the diversification of AI agents requires a variety of compute types, positioning AMD's CPU portfolio as the foundation for these workloads.

The processor complements the Helion agentic AI rack, an open-specification design arriving in November 2026. The Helion platform allows for configurations without GPUs to handle CPU-heavy agent tasks like code execution and tool calls, supporting up to 32,768 cores per rack via 128 EPYC "Venice" chips. Partners including Dell, HPE, Supermicro, and Cisco are supporting the rack, which includes a token router to direct requests to the most cost-effective AI models.

selectedTweets.text:
AMD just launched an AI rack that can ship with zero GPUs in it.

That's the tell. Helion, unveiled at OCP today:
• CPU-only version holds 128 EPYC "Venice" chips, up to 32,768 cores per rack (per Tom's Hardware)
• AMD says it's built for "agent execution," wired to separate inference hardware
• Dell, HPE, Supermicro, Hon Hai, Wiwynn, QCT, Lenovo and Cisco all signed on as partners
• AMD says configs are planned for November

Why would anyone want that? Because agents eat CPU. Tool calls, running code, spinning up sandboxes. That's mostly CPU work, not GPU work.

You can already see it in the supply chain. TrendForce has server CPU lead times at 25-30 weeks vs 16-20 in a normal market. Intel's CFO said the CPU-to-GPU ratio already went from 1:8 to 1:4, and could get to 1:1 as inference and agents grow.

Quick math: 1:8 to 1:1 is 8x the CPUs for the same GPU fleet. Most people still model CPUs as a rounding error in AI capex.

Last week I posted that OpenAI's in-house chip nodes run on AMD Turin hosts, not Nvidia's Vera. Now AMD is selling racks with no accelerator at all.

Don't stop at AMD though. More CPU sockets means more server DRAM to fill, and TrendForce says DRAM "stays very tight." And somebody has to build these racks. Wiwynn and Supermicro are on the list.

selectedTweets.quotedTweetText:
OPENAI'S JALAPEÑO ASIC RACKS RUN ON AMD EPYC TURIN, NOT NVIDIA VERA

- OpenAI's in-house Jalapeño chips are paired with AMD EPYC "Turin" host CPUs
- Each node carries 1.5 TB of memory
- OpenAI hardware head Richard Ho said Vera is "still a bit behind in maturity" and the pick was about cutting risk and speeding development
- He also noted Turin sits in a socket while Vera is board-mounted, so swaps are easier

Everyone frames custom ASICs as an Nvidia vs. Broadcom fight. The quiet part is the host CPU. Every ASIC rack still needs one, and the biggest lab just picked x86 over Nvidia's own CPU.

Also 1.5 TB per node is a lot of DRAM riding along with every ASIC deployment. Memory wins either way.

Ho left the door open to Vera or Arm later, so this isn't forever. But for now AMD gets paid on OpenAI's custom silicon too.
